text:
jess: Hey team, hitting a weird failure when onboarding a customer on Dedicated + private VPC. If I set REDWOOD_BASE_URL to the proxy endpoint and point REDWOOD_CUSTOM_CA_BUNDLE to our internal CA, the python async client fails TLS handshake :confused:

mika: ugh, can you paste the traceback? is this aiohttp or requests?

jess: aiohttp. traceback is basically `ssl.SSLCertVerificationError: certificate verify failed: self signed certificate in certificate chain`. Minimal reproducer:```python
from redwood import AsyncClient
client = AsyncClient(api_key="x", base_url="https://proxy.customer.example", custom_ca="/etc/ssl/certs/rdw.pem")
await client.generate("hello")
```
I tried env var `REDWOOD_CUSTOM_CA_BUNDLE=/etc/ssl/certs/rdw.pem` and also passing `ssl=True` but nothing changed.

sam: quick note: the async SDK uses aiohttp under the hood and we pass the `ssl` kw to TCPConnector. But we didn't wire the `custom_ca` param through in a couple of older constructors — easy oversight.

sam: workaround: create an SSLContext and pass it via `client._session` or monkeypatch a connector:```python
import ssl, aiohttp
ctx = ssl.create_default_context(cafile="/etc/ssl/certs/rdw.pem")
connector = aiohttp.TCPConnector(ssl=ctx)
session = aiohttp.ClientSession(connector=connector)
client = AsyncClient(...)
client._session = session  # gross but works for debug
```

jess: thanks. That works locally but not ideal for customers. Also noticed mypy complains: `AsyncClient.__init__` typing stub doesn't accept `custom_ca` or `base_url` as kwarg (our stubs are out of sync).

oliver: yeah, we accidentally regressed the typed signature in 0.9.x when we refactored. Two things: (1) runtime kwargs should be accepted (we accept **kwargs), (2) stubs need updating so static type checkers don't loudly fail.

mika: can we do a small patch to (A) accept `custom_ca`/`ca_bundle_path` in the AsyncClient ctor and forward it to aiohttp connector, (B) update typeshed/stubs? I can put up a PR.

jess: also observed auth retry behavior: when token refresh happens (401 -> refresh -> retry), the new request doesn't reapply the SSLContext from the original request binder, leading to intermittent cert failures on the retry. Repro is brittle but noticeable under load. :bug:

sam: that sounds like connector reuse causing the session to reset without the custom ssl set. Our retry logic re-creates the request object but reuses the default connector in some paths. I'll add a test that simulates a failing handshake then a successful path to validate.

mika: opened draft PR with two commits: "async: accept custom_ca and wire to aiohttp connector" and "types: update AsyncClient __init__ stub to include base_url/custom_ca". CI flagged a flake8 tweak.

ci-bot: build/pytest — running tests for pr/3147 (sam/mika)

oliver: small ask: add a short snippet in the onboarding sample-app that shows `export REDWOOD_CUSTOM_CA_BUNDLE=/path/to/ca.pem` + `export REDWOOD_BASE_URL=...` and mention the aiohttp caveat. New customers keep assuming `requests`-style `verify=` env behavior.

jess: yes please. Also add a note about private deployments needing outbound egress to CRL/OCSP endpoints or skip OCSP checks in the sample if the certs are internal.

sam: agreed. I'll also change retry code to reuse original connector/ssl context on retries and add a unit test. After that we should cut a patch release.

mika: thanks all. I'll keep the PR open for reviews, mark it as urgent for Dedicated onboarding.

jess: awesome :thumbsup: — adding a comment in the customer ticket linking this thread and the PR.
